articles.title: Staff desks at a glance
articles.summary: Which back-office desk handles which work, who can open it, and the runbook that governs it.
articles.html:
Important

Internal runbook. Visible to Draazy staff only.

Daily checklist

Monitor

  • Waiting for you tiles (staff dashboard): a number in amber means work is open on that desk.
  • The Oldest … line on each tile, for example "Oldest 3h ago": the tile with the oldest item goes first.
  • All clear is the only empty state. If the dashboard says it could not load, reload; do not assume nothing is waiting.
  • Managers and admins: SLA health shows the share of work finished inside target: Listing approval, Ticket pickup, Service delivery, Concierge → Live and (when Flatmates is on) Flatmate review. Green at 90% or more, amber 75–89%, rose below 75%, plus a late now count. View full analytics opens the SLA tab.
  • On a desktop, the chat button bottom-right shows how many support chats are waiting on us.

Work on

  • Open the tile with the oldest waiting item and follow its runbook from the table below.
  • Managers and admins: clear the Pending Verification, Needs Follow-up, Flagged Listings and Open Reports tiles under Needs attention.
  • No tile, or "No work is assigned to you yet"? Ask your manager to grant a function in Team & Access.

One back office

Staff, managers and admins share one back office. Managers and admins open it at /admin; staff open the same pages under /staff/…. Old /ops/… bookmarks redirect to the matching /admin/… page.

What you see depends on the functions you hold (KYC review, Property verification, Listing moderation, Post on behalf, Flatmates, Localities, Review moderation, Support, Enquiries, User lookup, Reports, Referrals, Refunds, Leads, Societies, Content, Analytics, and one per service desk). A staff member with no function sees the dashboard and Runbooks only. Admins see everything; managers hold every function by default, plus Team & Access. Finance, Settings, Integrations, Erasure requests, Help feedback and Error log are admin only. If a desk you need is missing, ask your manager or an admin to grant the function in Team & Access (/admin/team, manager and admin only) — do not borrow a colleague's login. New staff activate from an invite link at /staff-invite.

Desks

Desk Route Work Runbook
Support chats /admin/support One chat per customer, tagged by property, flatmate post, request, identity check or payment Support chats
Service tickets each service desk's Customer tickets tab; Home Loans (/admin/home-loans) is the board Internal service tickets, escalation and P0 handling Chats, tickets and escalation
Leads /admin/leads Sales leads: claim, call, log outcomes, convert Leads CRM
KYC review /admin/kyc-review ID + selfie identity checks Identity review
Rent Agreement /admin/rent-agreement Rent-agreement drafting, registration, refunds Drafting desk and service queues
Other service desks /admin/legal, /admin/interior, /admin/packers, /admin/valuation Legal, interior, packers and valuation requests Service queues
Referrals /admin/referrals Referral reward review and clawbacks Referral fraud review
Refunds /admin/refunds Pass and contact-pack refund requests, automatic refunds, disputes Refunds desk
Flatmates /admin/flatmates Flatmate posts, badges, edits and group applications Flatmate review
Properties /admin/properties Listing verification, re-checks, duplicates Verification SLAs
Properties → ownership /admin/properties Ownership evidence and ownership badges Ownership and badges
Reports /admin/reports Listing, user and flatmate reports; review moderation Reports and takedowns
Places /admin/places Areas, duplicate societies, society details Society moderation, Localities desk
Post on Behalf /admin/post-on-behalf Listings for owners who called or messaged Post on behalf
Enquiries /admin/enquiries Enquiries, visits and deals Enquiries desk
Content /admin/content FAQs and site content Content (FAQs)
Finance /admin/finance Revenue and payments (admin only) Finance desk
Users /admin/users Account lookup and actions Users desk
Team Activity /admin/staff-activity What each staff member handled Team activity
Team & Access, Settings, Integrations /admin/team, /admin/settings, /admin/integrations Staff and functions; flags and maps; outside services Team and access, Settings and integrations

Rules for every desk

  • Work the oldest item in the queue first unless a runbook says a risk queue goes first.
  • Record why you decided, not just what — the next reviewer reads your note, not your mind.
  • Never decide a case you raised, approved or claimed yourself where the runbook asks for a second person.
  • Never move a case to WhatsApp, personal email or chat; keep it on the desk.
  • When a desk fails to load, treat the queue as unknown, not empty, and escalate.

articles.title: Daily routine - start and end of shift
articles.summary: What to check when you start a shift, how to use the Dashboard, the notification bell and Ctrl+K search, and how to hand over at the end.
articles.html:
Important

Internal runbook. Visible to Draazy staff only.

Daily checklist

Monitor

  • The Dashboard when you sign in. Staff see Your work. Managers and admins see the platform Dashboard.
  • Every tile that is not All clear. Amber means something is waiting.
  • The notification bell (red dot). It lights for notes sent to you and owner replies.
  • The Oldest age on each of your queue tiles, not just the count.
  • A dark notice on the bell or a tile that did not load. That means unknown, not empty.

Work on

  • Your queue tiles first, oldest item first.
  • Owner replies in the bell, so listings are not left waiting on you.
  • Desks that have no tile (see the note below the table). Open them yourself.
  • Anything you left half done yesterday.
  • A short note on every case you could not finish, before you sign off.

Desk and access

  • Everyone in the panel can open the Dashboard. No function is needed.
  • Staff sign in at /staff/.... Managers and admins use /admin/.... Links in the bell and search switch to the right one for you.
  • A staff member with no function sees only the Dashboard. Ask your manager to grant a function in Team & Access.
  • A desk you cannot open is hidden. That is by design, not a fault.

The staff Dashboard ("Your work")

The header says Your work and your name. A 7 days / 30 days toggle changes the "handled" numbers.

Part What it tells you
Waiting for you tile Open items for one function. Shows the count (amber if above 0) and Oldest age, or All clear. Click it to open the desk.
You handled N How many items you handled in the chosen period, per function.
"No work is assigned to you yet." You have no function. Ask your manager.
"Your functions have no queue to work." Your functions have no tile. Open their desks directly.

Tiles exist only for these desks:

Function What the tile counts
KYC review Pending identity reviews
Property verification Pending property reviews and ownership (Verified property) requests
Listing moderation Pending listings
Support Support chats with an unread customer message, not resolved or closed
Reports Reports that are open or in review
Review moderation Reviews awaiting moderation
Enquiries Contact requests still pending
Flatmates Flatmate posts, rooms, groups and group applications awaiting review, plus edited posts waiting for a re-check
Societies Member-added societies not yet merged or archived
Each service desk Open service requests (not awaiting payment, draft shared, action required, completed or cancelled) and open, in-progress or waiting tickets

A tile with a count but no Oldest age reads Waiting. No tile exists for Users, Content, Localities, Analytics, Refunds, Referrals, Leads or Post on behalf. The Flatmates tile does not count Badge requests. If you hold one of these, open the desk at the start of the shift and look for yourself.

The manager and admin Dashboard

  • SLA health (only if you have analytics access): Listing approval 24h, Ticket pickup 4h, Service delivery 3d, Concierge to live 7d, Flatmate review 24h. Green is 90% or more on time, amber 75-89%, red below 75%. Grey Not recorded means no data. View full analytics opens the SLA tab.
  • Needs attention: Pending Verification, Needs Follow-up, Flagged Listings, Open Reports, New Enquiries, Scheduled Visits, Open Service Requests, Deals in Progress, Flatmate Posts to Review, Flatmate Reports, Unanswered Flatmate Requests (pending over 48h). Each opens its desk.
  • At a glance: Total Users, Active Listings, Deals closed (30d), Signups today, Visits today. Revenue (last 30 days) shows for admins only. A Flatmates row adds Live Rooms, Active Seekers, Matches (30d) and Host Reply Rate (30d); the last two open the Flatmates analytics tab.
  • Latest activity: oldest pending verifications (5 rows, View all) and the latest service requests.
  • A tile is hidden when you cannot open its desk. A tile at 0 reads All clear.

Notification bell

Click the bell in the top bar.

Section Meaning
For you Notes and alerts sent to you. Mark all read clears them.
Owner replied An owner answered a verification question. Opens that listing.
Pending verification Listings waiting for a check. Up to 5 shown.
Open service requests Requests waiting on a desk. Up to 5 shown.
  • The red dot only lights for For you and Owner replied. Queues are work, not news, so they do not light it.
  • It refreshes when you open it and about every 90 seconds while the tab is visible.
  • All caught up. means nothing is waiting.
  • This bell is not counting anything here. or Part of this bell is dark here. means a count failed. Open Properties and the service desks, which are the record.
  • Queues show only if you can open Properties or Tickets.

Desk alerts

For you also gets automatic desk alerts. A sweep runs every 15 minutes and sends each alert once. Staff accounts also get each alert by email, at the email on their account, unless Email is off in their notification settings. Managers and admins get the bell only.

Alert When Who gets it
New … An unassigned item arrived in the last hour, or a customer approved or asked for changes on a draft The person handling it, else everyone holding that desk's function
Waiting … The item passed its reminder time The person handling it, else everyone holding the function
Escalated … The item passed its escalation time Managers (admins if there are none)
Queue Reminder Escalation
Listing review, re-check of an edited live listing 24h 36h
Owner reply, ID check, identity appeal, flatmate check, refund request, verified-badge request 48h 72h
Unassigned service request 4h 8h
Support chat waiting on us (the alert reads "support ticket"), abuse report, flatmate post 24h 48h
Rent agreement the stage deadline 1.5 × the stage deadline
Customer draft decision, community society New alert only —
Data-erasure request (admins only) 7d 20d
  • Several items on one desk arrive as one alert ("3 listings to review"). It opens the queue; a single item opens the item.
  • An ID check you claimed sends its alerts to you while your claim holds.
  • Refund requests send no New alert, only reminders and escalations.
  • A paid rent agreement waiting on the tenant sends no alert. The desk cannot act until the tenant fills their part.
  • Once the item is handled, its unread alert marks itself read. You do not need to clear it.
  • No function holder for a desk means its alerts go straight to managers.

Search (Ctrl+K)

Press Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on Mac) on a computer to jump to the search box. On a phone, tap the search icon in the top bar. Press Esc to close.

  • Type at least 2 characters. Chips: All, Features, Listings, People.
  • Results: Pages, Features, Listings and People. Listings need Properties access. People need Users access.
  • Every runbook is searchable under Features. Type its title.
  • A notice that part of the search did not answer means some results are missing. Try again.

Start of shift

  1. Open the Dashboard. Note any tile that is not All clear.
  2. Open the bell. Read For you and Owner replied.
  3. Open your first desk from the tile, oldest item first.
  4. Open desks with no tile.
  5. If something looks wrong or old, follow the escalation rules in the staff desks runbook.

End of shift

  1. Finish or release what you hold. Do not leave a case claimed and untouched.
  2. Write a short note on each open case: what you did, what is left, who is waiting.
  3. Check Owner replied and your queue tiles once more.
  4. Tell your manager about anything stuck, old or unclear. The panel has no handover button, so say it in a note or message.
  5. Do not say "all clear" if a tile or the bell was dark. Say it could not be counted.

Never do

  • Never treat a failed or dark count as zero.
  • Never skip the desks that have no tile.
  • Never share your password or recovery codes to cover a shift. Ask your manager for access.
  • Never leave customer details in notes. Write only what the next person needs.

Related

  • Staff desks
  • Verification and SLA
  • Ticket escalation
  • Identity review
  • Reports and takedowns

articles.title: Verification SLAs
articles.summary: Internal queue rules for listing verification, live re-checks, duplicates and owner follow-up.
articles.html:
Important

Internal runbook. Visible to Draazy staff only.

Daily checklist

Monitor

  • To verify tab, newest first — amber at 24 h ("due soon"), rose at 48 h ("overdue").
  • Re-checks and Badge requests tabs — amber at 24 h, rose at 72 h.
  • Flagged tab count — every flagged listing is out of search until you clear or archive it.
  • Duplicates tab count — clusters still waiting for a decision.
  • Follow-up tab count — live listings the owner has not confirmed for over two weeks. It has no amber or rose.
  • Your bell alerts (also emailed to staff): New …, Waiting … and Escalated: … for the queues in "Queue alerts and escalations" below.
  • Every queue shows newest first, and each tile shows when the listing was created or last updated.

Work on

  • Clear the rose rows in To verify first; they sit at the end of the list. Use the Awaiting owner chip to separate staff-posted listings that only need an owner nudge.
  • Decide every row in Re-checks: Looks fine, or take the listing down.
  • Grant or decline every request in Badge requests.
  • Decide each cluster in Duplicates before approving any member.
  • On Follow-up, send the WhatsApp reminder (bell icon) and record it.

Desk and access

Use Admin → Properties (/admin/properties) for listing verification. Staff open it under /staff/properties. Access comes from functions: Property verification (properties:verify) decides verification cases; Listing moderation (properties:moderate) flags, archives, restores and merges duplicates. Either one lets you edit a listing during review.

Use the owner follow-up buttons only with the Post on behalf function (postOnBehalf:write); those routes can prepare claim-link and WhatsApp outreach to an owner.

Queue tabs and targets

Tab What enters Target shown in the desk
To verify Pending listings ready for staff review; staff-posted listings waiting on the owner sit here under the Awaiting owner progress chip Warn at 24 hours; breach at 48 hours
Re-checks Live listings with a recheckRequestedAt timestamp Warn at 24 hours; breach at 72 hours
Badge requests Listings asking for ownership verification Warn at 24 hours; breach at 72 hours
Follow-up Live listings the owner has not confirmed as still available for over two weeks No breach colour; the row is a follow-up task
Flagged Listings with a staff flag Work by risk, not by SLA colour
Duplicates Server-built duplicate clusters Decide each cluster before approving any member
All listings Full moderation view, including archived rows when filtered Use only to find or restore a known listing

The SLA panel is green at 90% or better, amber from 75% to 89%, and rose below 75%.

Queue alerts and escalations

You do not have to watch the tabs all day. A sweep runs every 15 minutes and sends a bell alert for each queue below. On a staff account the same alert is also emailed to the address on the account (managers and admins get the bell only).

Alert When Goes to
New … (arrival) A new item arrives unassigned, in the first hour Staff holding the function
Waiting 24h+ (reminder) The item has waited the reminder time The assignee, or the staff holding the function
Escalated: … untouched 36h+ The item has waited the escalation time Managers (admins if there are no managers)
Queue Reminder Escalation Function that gets it
Listing to review 24h 36h Listing moderation
Listing re-check 24h 36h Listing moderation
Owner reply to answer 48h 72h Property verification
Verified-badge request 48h 72h Property verification
ID check, identity appeal 48h 72h KYC review
Flatmate check 48h 72h Flatmates
Flatmate post to moderate 24h 48h Flatmates
Support chat waiting on us 24h 48h Support
Abuse report 24h 48h Reports
Refund request 48h 72h Refunds
Unassigned service request 4h 8h That service desk
Rent agreement Past its stage deadline 1.5 times the stage deadline Rent Agreement desk
Data-erasure request 7 days 20 days Admins
Customer draft decision, community society Arrival alert only None The desk or Societies

An alert clears itself when the item is decided. Fix the queue, not the alert. A rent agreement that waits on the tenant's payment invite is shown as waiting, not late. Real alert emails need email delivery switched on in Settings and integrations.

The tab colours above (24h/48h, 24h/72h) are the desk's own colours; the bell alerts use the times in this table. Suspended accounts stop receiving alerts.

Listing states

State Staff meaning Buyer-visible effect
pending Waiting, in review, or awaiting owner info Hidden from public search
approved Published Visible unless archived
needs_info review Staff asked for a correction Listing stays pending; owner sees the reason
rejected Refusal Hidden; the owner's edit returns a fixable rejection to pending, Reopen for review returns any rejection
flagged Unsafe or disputed Hidden until the flag is cleared or archived
archived Soft-deleted Hidden; restore returns to pending

Review procedure

  1. Open the listing from To verify or Re-checks.
  2. Check the photos, duplicate result, details, address and locality.
  3. Tick every checklist item before approving. The Approve button stays locked until the checklist is complete, and the server rejects incomplete approvals.
  4. Read fraud signals before deciding. Hard signals stay visible as warnings; weigh them, then decide yourself.
  5. Add an internal note when the decision depends on evidence not visible in the fields.
  6. Decide with Approve, Needs info, or Reject.

Decision rules

Approve listing

Use Approve only when the checklist is complete, you have weighed any duplicate or broker signal, and the address and locality are believable. One approval is final; you cannot approve a listing you posted or own.

Send needs info

Use Needs info for fixable gaps. Choose a reason code. If the code is other, write the note. Owner reply or edit resubmits the listing and clears the waiting flag.

The hourly sweep sends owner reminders after 3 days and 7 days. If there is no reply or edit after 14 days, the listing is soft-archived with needs_info_timeout.

Reject listing

A reason code is required. Five reasons are fixable: photos not real, wrong details, locality unclear, document unreadable and name mismatch. The owner is told to edit the listing and resubmit it, and the edit sends it back to pending for a fresh decision. The other reasons (duplicate, broker, RERA, other) are final: the owner cannot edit, and an owner reply does not reopen the listing. Use Reopen for review when a finally rejected case must re-enter review.

Work re-checks while live

Use Approve edits or the re-check pass action when the live listing still matches policy. Use Reject listing from the re-check modal when the live listing must come down; rejecting removes it from public search.

Resolve duplicate clusters

Use Keep this, archive the rest only when the cluster really points to the same property. Use Not a duplicate for false positives. Treat a duplicate-scan failure or truncation as unknown, not clean.

Never do in listing verification

  • Do not approve with an unticked checklist.
  • Do not approve a listing you posted or own.
  • Do not use Reject for a fixable photo, address or document gap.
  • Do not publish a staff-posted listing before the owner confirms it.
  • Do not treat Follow-up as a breach queue; send the owner nudge and record the outreach.

Escalation path

Escalate suspected organised fraud, legal or police references, minors, media contact, or repeated attempts to reopen rejected listings up the ladder in Chats, tickets and escalation, by phone for a P0. Record the listing id, reason code, signals and action already taken.

Related

  • Chats, tickets and escalation
  • Support chats
  • Ownership and badges
  • Reports and takedowns

articles.title: Chats, tickets and escalation
articles.summary: How staff tell a support chat, a desk case and an internal service ticket apart, and how to escalate each one.

headings.text: Chat, desk case or service ticket

articles.html:
Important

Internal runbook. Visible to Draazy staff only.

Daily checklist

Monitor

  • Support chats → Waiting on us count: customers whose last message nobody has answered. See Support chats.
  • On desktop, the chat button bottom-right shows the same count on every staff page.
  • Every desk's Customer tickets tab (and the Home Loans board): the age chip turns amber at 2 days open and rose at 5 days.
  • P0 reports: money paid to someone claiming to be Draazy, a physical threat, or contact from police or a regulator.

Work on

  • Answer Waiting on us chats first.
  • Phone the ops lead for any P0 report; do not rely on a chat or ticket alone.
  • On Home Loans, Claim unassigned tickets, press Start when you begin and Resolve when done.
  • Set a ticket to Waiting only when the next step is the customer's.
  • Escalate with the chat link or ticket id, what you checked and what you told the customer.

Chat, desk case or service ticket

Three different things share the word "ticket" in old habits. They are not the same.

Thing Purpose Lives in Customer sees it
Support chat People talking. One chat per customer, every message tagged About a property, flatmate post, request, payment, identity check or General. Has an owner, no priority, SLA or money /admin/support and the dock Yes, as the "Draazy support" chat
Desk case Work with a decision: approve a listing, verify identity, draft an agreement, refund Its own desk Its status, yes
Service ticket Internal lead for a service team, with team, assignee and private notes The Customer tickets tab on each service desk, and the Home Loans board No. The customer is never notified

Customers do not file support tickets; they write in the chat, and desks link to it with Chat with customer instead of hosting their own thread. A service enquiry form (a service page or the Move-in Pack) does open a service ticket for that team on its own.

Never paste private notes into a chat. If a chat needs tracked work for a service team, press Service ticket in the chat header (Support access only), pick the team, add a subject and optional note, then Create ticket.

Who can open what

Surface Route Access
Support chats /admin/support Support function, manager or admin sees everything; a desk function sees only its own topics (see Support chats)
Customer tickets tab each service desk page (?view=tickets) tickets:read, held through the Support or Home Loans function. Staff see their own desk's tickets; admins and managers see every desk
Home Loans board /admin/home-loans The Home Loans function

Staff open these pages under /staff/….

Service ticket queue

Open the desk page and switch to Customer tickets (?view=tickets; Home Loans needs no switch). It has search, Priority and Date chips, Export CSV, and a ?open=<ticketId> deep link.

Field Current behavior
Team Staff are server-scoped to their own team; admins and managers can see all teams
Priority Shown as a badge (low, medium, high or urgent) with a Priority filter. The screens have no priority editor, and tickets raised from a chat use the default
Assignee Staff self-claim; admins and managers can assign to an active staff member on the ticket team
Notes Private internal notes appended with Add / Save; customers never see them
Age Non-terminal tickets show today, 2–4 day warning, or 5+ day breach

Service-ticket actions

Button or control Effect
Claim Assigns the ticket to you; status stays open
Start Admin console assigns first active team member if unassigned, then sets in-progress
Resolve Sets resolved
Open Opens the drawer/modal without mutating
Status select Can set open, in-progress, waiting, resolved, or closed
Activity / Add a note Appends one private note

There is no transition table for service-request tickets; any legal status can be set from any other. Use waiting only when the next action is genuinely the customer's. Use closed for filed work where no resolution step is needed.

Priority on service tickets

The backend accepts low, medium, high and urgent, but the ticket screens do not send priority changes. If the shown priority is wrong, record the real impact in a private note and escalate to the support lead or ops lead. For a P0 report, phone the ops lead immediately.

Drafting-desk relationship

A service ticket is a hand-off row, not the work itself. The service desk pages (/admin/rent-agreement, /admin/legal, and so on) own the live service-request workflow: documents, identity reveal, drafts, customer approval, refunds, registration and cancellation. When a ticket points to a rent agreement or other service request, do the workflow on its desk and keep the ticket note as the staff hand-off trail.

Handling procedure

  1. Identify what you are looking at: a support chat, a desk case, or a service ticket.
  2. Read the whole chat, case or ticket before replying or moving status.
  3. Check the account, listing, invoice, service request or verification case.
  4. Write customer-facing text only in the chat or the case's own customer message. Use private notes only on service tickets and desk notes.
  5. If a screen fails to load, retry or escalate the outage; never treat an error as an empty queue.
  6. Close with the outcome, not with "resolved".

Auto-escalate to P0

Auto-escalate reports of money paid to someone claiming to represent Draazy, physical threat or harassment involving a visit, a payment charged with no invoice record, or contact from law enforcement or a regulator.

P0 goes to the ops lead by phone, not by assignment alone.

Escalation ladder

Agent → Support lead → Ops lead → Trust & Safety for fraud or safety, Finance for money → Legal.

Every hop must include the chat link or ticket id, what you checked, what you told the customer, and why the next team owns it.

Refund handling

Support chats cannot approve or process refunds. A chat can only collect the customer's request and keep them updated.

For rent-agreement refunds, send the case to the Rent Agreement desk: the holder asks for the refund and a manager approves it before the gateway refund is sent. For other paid products, use the Refunds desk or escalate to Finance with the transaction id and policy reason. Do not quote an internal cap or promise money back before the desk confirms the path.

What never to do

  • Never share another user's contact details, even to connect two parties
  • Never confirm or deny whether a specific person has an account
  • Never quote internal SLA figures to a consumer
  • Never take a case to WhatsApp; keep it in the chat
  • Never tell a customer nobody is waiting when the screen says it could not load
  • Never approve a refund from a chat
  • Never put staff-only notes in a chat reply; the customer reads it

  • Drafting desk and service queues
  • Service queues
  • Verification SLAs
  • Identity review

articles.title: Identity review
articles.summary: Internal KYC desk procedure for reviewing captured ID documents, selfies, appeals and revocations.
articles.html:
Important

Internal runbook. Visible to Draazy staff only.

Daily checklist

Monitor

  • Needs review tab, newest first — amber from 24 h ("due soon"), rose from 48 h ("overdue"). Each row shows when the case was created or last updated.
  • Overdue button count: pending cases past 48 h.
  • Claim chips (All, Unclaimed, Mine n/3, Others): you can hold at most 3 cases at once.
  • Appeals tab count: rejected applicants who asked for a second look. These also raise a staff alert.
  • A pending case left for 14 days is rejected automatically, so keep the oldest moving.

Work on

  • Clear Overdue cases first, then work the rest of Needs review.
  • Answer every open Appeals case: uphold the rejection or reopen it for a fresh review.
  • Finish a case you open: opening it holds it for you for 30 minutes.
  • Decide each case from the evidence in it; never your own case.

Desk and access

Use KYC review at /admin/kyc-review (staff open it under /staff/kyc-review). It belongs to the KYC review function; the page needs identity:write (there is no view-only version), which covers viewing, claiming, approving, rejecting and revoking.

The customer submits a camera-captured identity document image and selfie through the identity flow. Review only what the case shows; do not ask for documents outside the product flow.

A row opens one case in a window: document images and what the applicant entered on the left, the selfie and pose below, History collapsed, and every action in the rail on the right. Next case moves to the next case you can take; Refresh links renews the image links. A case someone else holds opens read-only with no decide forms. Duplicate warnings (the same document on another account) show above the images.

Edit account under the applicant's entries changes the account name or email. Use it only to fix a clear typo.

Queue tabs

Tab What it contains Sort and page size
Needs review Pending identity submissions Newest first; 10 per page
Appeals Rejected cases the applicant asked to have checked again; tagged Appeal Newest first; 10 per page
Decided Verified, rejected and revoked cases Newest first; 10 per page

Filters: name or mobile, document type and the Date chips (All, Today, 7d, 30d) on every tab; Claim and Overdue on Needs review; Outcome (Verified, Rejected, Revoked) on Decided. Clear filters resets them. Filters reset when you change tab. The list is always newest first.

Targets and stale handling

Item Rule
Warning age The UI marks old pending cases amber at 24 hours
Overdue filter The backend counts pending cases as overdue at 48 hours
Claim hold Opening a pending case claims it for 30 minutes
Active claims A reviewer may hold 3 active identity cases
Stale pending sweep Cases older than 14 days are rejected as not_reviewed; images are purged and the attempt window is reset

Force release is admin-only. Use it only when another reviewer has clearly abandoned a claim; managers and staff ask an admin. The button asks for confirmation before clearing the hold. You cannot decide your own identity case.

Approval checklist

Approve only after all of these are true:

  1. Every visible checklist item is ticked.
  2. The document number is present.
  3. The holder name is present.
  4. Either full date of birth or birth year is present; never both.
  5. The holder is at least 18.
  6. Birth year is between 1900 and the allowed adult cutoff.
  7. The selfie and document holder match.
  8. If a liveness challenge exists, Confirm the requested pose is ticked.

Type the document number, holder name and date of birth (or tick Year only (old Aadhaar) and enter the birth year) from the image, and pick the gender on the document. If your number does not match the applicant's entry you are asked to re-check; tick the override only when you read it from the image and the applicant's entry was wrong. The case then shows Number corrected by reviewer. Approving sets the account name to the holder name you confirmed.

Use Approve review only when the button is enabled. An approval is final; there is no second check.

Rejection rules

Use Reject review for cases that cannot pass from the submitted evidence. Pick one reason:

Reason Use when
blurry Text or face cannot be read
cropped Required document area is missing
mismatch Selfie, name or number does not match
expired Document is no longer valid
not_holder Submitter is not the document holder
unsupported Document type is outside the accepted set
other The case is invalid for another visible reason

Write a note of at least 10 characters for mismatch, not_holder and other.

Appeals

When a rejected applicant asks for a second look, the case appears under Appeals with their note.

  • Uphold rejection closes the appeal and the rejection stands.
  • Reopen for review sends the case back to Needs review for a fresh decision. It is offered only while the photos are still stored; once they are purged the appeal can only be upheld.
  • You cannot decide an appeal on your own identity case.

Revocation

Use Revoke or Revoke badge only when the verified badge should be removed. Revocation needs a reason between 10 and 300 characters and is audited.

An identity-earned verified badge cannot be withdrawn from the user badge screen. Revoke it from the identity review record.

Never do in identity review

  • Do not ask an admin to force-release an active colleague unless needed to keep the queue moving.
  • Do not accept a typed document value that contradicts the captured image.
  • Do not store copies of the captured document or selfie outside the case.

Related

  • Chats, tickets and escalation
  • Verification SLAs
  • Ownership and badges
  • Referral fraud review

articles.title: Ownership and badges
articles.summary: Internal procedure for ownership evidence, the Verified property badge and manual KYC done badges.

headings.text: Never do in ownership and badges

articles.html:
Important

Internal runbook. Visible to Draazy staff only.

Daily checklist

Monitor

  • Badge requests tab in Properties: "due soon" (amber) from 24 h, "overdue" (rose) from 72 h, oldest first.
  • Owner is seeking the Verified property badge banner: the request waits for your answer.
  • Current or Expired chip on each evidence row: only current proof counts.

Work on

  • Answer every badge request: Grant ownership verification, or Decline badge request with a reason.
  • Open every evidence row and compare the dates and address with the listing before you grant.
  • Withdraw a granted badge when its evidence becomes unsafe.

Desks and access

Draazy shows two badges only. Verified property is the ownership badge, granted here. KYC done is the person badge, earned through Identity review or granted by hand in Users. Neither certifies legal title.

Review ownership evidence inside Admin → Properties (/admin/properties) in the listing review modal; staff open it under /staff/properties. You need the Property verification function (properties:verify). Use the Ownership verification section to read and record evidence, then grant, or withdraw a grant. Decline a badge request from the banner. The verdict strip shows Ownership verified with the date it is valid until, or the missing evidence that blocks it.

Hand-granted KYC done badges live in Admin → Users (/admin/users). A manager or admin with users:write uses Grant Verified badge or Remove Verified badge with a reason, and it takes effect at once. You cannot badge yourself. Every grant and removal is audited.

Ownership request states

State Staff action User-visible effect
No request Request more evidence or leave untouched No ownership badge
Requested Inspect evidence and decide Listing can still be reviewed separately
Granted Grant ownership verification Ownership badge appears on eligible reads
Declined Decline badge request → Decline request No ownership badge; owner sees the reason
Withdrawn Withdraw ownership verification (reason required) Badge is removed; evidence rows remain

Ownership review is separate from listing publication. Recording evidence does not grant a badge; staff must click Grant ownership verification. The button stays disabled while evidence is missing (Record the missing evidence first.) and while the owner has not got KYC done (Owner ID pending: verify the owner's ID first.). Verify the owner in Identity review, then come back.

A granted badge lapses when the documents expire, until the owner submits current ones. It is also removed if the listing's address, society or electricity meter number is changed later, until the listing is re-checked.

Where badge requests come from

The owner uploads a proof to the listing's Document Vault and taps Request Verified badge. An upload alone queues nothing. The request lands in the Badge requests tab of /admin/properties, and the review modal opens with the banner Owner is seeking the Verified property badge.

Answer every request one way or the other: grant in the badge section, or use Decline badge request on the banner. A decline needs a reason of up to 300 characters, which the owner sees, and leaves the listing's status untouched, so it works on a live, paused or pending listing.

Evidence rules

Listing Required ownership evidence
Rent Address proof or title proof
Sale Title proof

Accepted title proofs are Index II, share certificate, Satbara / 7-12 extract, 8A extract and property card. Accepted address proofs are tax receipt and electricity bill. Power of attorney proves authority only when the subject name is present. Site photos and sale deed are supporting evidence, not enough alone.

Aadhaar and PAN are retired identity evidence for this desk. Do not accept them as ownership proof.

A RERA number is shared by the owner: check it on MahaRERA with the review modal's Open MahaRERA search link and tick the RERA check. Draazy does not verify societies, so a society name or share certificate is evidence about the flat, not a society approval.

Date and document checks

  1. Open every evidence row before deciding.
  2. Confirm the vault category matches the evidence type.
  3. Confirm issuedOn is present, not in the future and not later than the uploaded file.
  4. Apply the validity window: land records, property card and electricity bill are valid for 90 days; site photos are valid for 180 days; tax receipt is valid until the financial year end.
  5. Compare the property address, society, flat or survey identifiers against the listing.
  6. Confirm the reviewer is not the listing owner.

Ownership decisions

Use Grant ownership verification when required evidence is valid and matches the listing. Use Decline request when evidence is missing, unreadable, mismatched or category-invalid. Use Withdraw ownership verification when a granted badge becomes unsafe.

Do not use listing approval as a shortcut for ownership proof. A listing can be live without ownership verification.

Manual KYC done badges

A manager or admin grants or removes a manual KYC done badge in one step:

Rule Requirement
Who A manager or admin with users:write
Reason Required, 10 to 300 characters
Self You cannot badge your own account
Already verified A second grant is refused

Use this panel only for hand-granted badges. If the badge was earned through KYC, revoke through Identity review.

Never do in ownership and badges

  • Do not grant ownership from Aadhaar, PAN or a selfie.
  • Do not grant ownership when only supporting evidence is present.
  • Do not grant a manual badge to your own account.
  • Do not withdraw an identity-earned badge from the user badge panel.
  • Do not delete evidence rows to hide a bad decision; withdraw or decline instead.

Related

  • Verification SLAs
  • Identity review
  • Chats, tickets and escalation

articles.title: Reports and takedowns
articles.summary: Internal trust and safety procedure for report triage, chat reports, takedowns and dismissals.

headings.text: Never do in reports and takedowns

articles.html:
Important

Internal runbook. Visible to Draazy staff only.

Daily checklist

Monitor

  • Tab counts on Properties, Users & owners and Flatmate posts: reports not yet decided.
  • Open status chip: nobody has decided it. Being reviewed may be with a colleague.
  • A red 3x badge or higher: three or more reports hit the same target. Treat it as an escalation signal.
  • Reviews tab, if you hold the Review moderation function: pending reviews to approve or reject.

Work on

  • Filter Open and read View details before you act on any report.
  • Choose Take down, Suspend, Resolve or Dismiss; a prompt asks for an optional internal note. Add one when the reason is not obvious.
  • Use Bulk Resolve or Bulk Dismiss (after Select all open or ticking rows) only on clearly no-action reports.
  • On Reviews, Approve or Reject each pending review.

Desk and access

Use Admin → Reports (/admin/reports, page title Reports & Moderation) for Trust & Safety triage. You need the Reports function (reports:read to view, reports:write to decide); staff open it under /staff/reports. The Reviews tab needs the separate Review moderation function.

Users can file listing reports, user reports and review reports. Chat can open a Report user modal for one-to-one conversations; group conversations do not expose user blocking or reporting.

Queue tabs and filters

Tab Target types Available enforcement
Properties Property listings Take down with hide_content
Users & owners User or owner account reports Suspend with suspend_account
Flatmate posts Rooms, groups and seeker posts Take down with hide_content
Reviews User reviews on listings and societies Approve / Reject (not a report; see below)

Filter by Status chips, reason and Reported date range, or search "Item, reason or note". Check whether a filter is hiding rows before you decide a queue is clear. Export CSV downloads the rows in the current tab; the reporter shows as Withheld.

Report states

Server state Staff label Rule
open Open Can be decided
reviewing Being reviewed Can be filtered; another moderator may be handling it
actioned Action taken Terminal
dismissed Dismissed Terminal

The UI label Resolve sends a reviewed-no-action decision that stores as dismissed. A terminal report cannot be reopened; file a fresh report if the problem recurs.

Triage procedure

  1. Open View details before acting.
  2. Read the reason, target title, target type and any repeat-target badge.
  3. Treat an Nx badge (N = 3 or more) as an escalation signal; it means that many reports hit the same target.
  4. Compare the report against the target in its owning desk before taking it down.
  5. Choose Take down, Suspend, Resolve or Dismiss. Bulk Resolve and Bulk Dismiss act on the rows you tick; use them only for clearly no-action reports.
  6. Write an internal note when the decision is not obvious from the reason and target.

Reporter identity is withheld from the queue and export. Use Withheld in notes; do not call the reporter anonymous if the system withheld them.

Enforcement effects

Button Backend effect
Take down on listing Flags the listing and removes it from public search
Suspend on user Suspends or archives the user through admin user enforcement
Take down on flatmate post Sets the post to removed; the author is not suspended
Resolve Stores a dismissed report with reviewed-no-action wording
Dismiss Stores a dismissed report without enforcement

The Reviews tab is a moderation list, not reports: filter Pending / Published / Rejected, search "Author, item or text", and use Approve (publishes) or Reject (hides the text and drops it from the rating). It shows only to accounts that hold the Review moderation function.

Chat blocks and reports

Blocking in Messages is pair-only. It prevents messaging both ways for that pair and can be undone with unblock. Deleting a message hides it only for the current user.

Use chat user reports like any other user report: inspect the target, look for repeat reports, and suspend only when account-level action is justified.

A customer writing to staff in Support is a support chat, not a report. If it describes abuse, ask them to use the report option on the listing, user or post so it lands here.

Never do in reports and takedowns

  • Do not reopen a decided report.
  • Do not expose reporter identity in a note or export.
  • Do not use account suspension for content that only needs content removal.
  • Do not use Resolve for an unsafe target just because another desk must finish the action.
  • Do not promise society enforcement unless the Societies desk reflects the action.

Related

  • Support chats
  • Chats, tickets and escalation
  • Verification SLAs
  • Flatmate review

articles.title: Society moderation
articles.summary: Internal procedure for duplicate society merges and society detail edits.
articles.html:
Important

Internal runbook. Visible to Draazy staff only.

Daily checklist

Monitor

  • Duplicates tab count: new societies waiting for a check.
  • Similar to row: Could not check means search by hand before merging; No obvious match means nothing similar was found.
  • Merged duplicates list at the bottom of Duplicates: recent merges you may need to undo.

Work on

  • Go through Duplicates and Merge only true duplicates of an existing society.
  • Undo a merge that was wrong.
  • In Society details, press Edit only when a society's details are wrong.

Desk and access

Use Places (/admin/places), tabs Duplicates and Society details. You need the Societies function (societies:read to view, societies:write for merges and detail edits); staff open it under /staff/places. The old /admin/societies link redirects there. The Areas tab on the same page belongs to the Localities desk and needs its own function.

A society is identified by its Google Maps place. Owners and seekers can only pick a society from Google Maps suggestions, so every society row maps to one real place. New societies are accepted only inside the districts served (see Settings and integrations).

Console tabs

Tab Use it for Primary actions
Duplicates Societies added from Google Maps picks, with duplicate hints. Search by society or locality Merge, Undo
Society details Search by society or builder and edit data Google does not have: Registered, Conveyance done, Maintenance (₹/sqft) and an Admin note Edit, then Save

If a queue fails to load, a red banner says so with Retry. That is missing data, not an empty queue.

Merge decisions

Use Merge when a candidate duplicates an existing canonical society. The merge window searches target societies ("Search societies…") and confirms with Merge. Its listings, follows and reviews then read on the society you merged into; nothing is deleted.

Use Undo only when the merged-away society should exist again. Duplicate hints are advisory; if suggestions are checking, failed or absent, search manually before merging.

Registered and Conveyance done are staff-entered details, not a Draazy check. Do not describe a society as verified. For RERA, say it is shared by the owner and to check it on MahaRERA.

Never do in society moderation

  • Do not merge a candidate just because names are similar.
  • Do not use Society details edits to hide a moderation problem.

Related

  • Reports and takedowns
  • Localities desk
  • Support chats

articles.title: Post on behalf
articles.summary: Internal procedure for creating an owner listing from a call or WhatsApp handoff.

headings.text: Never do in post on behalf

articles.html:
Important

Internal runbook. Visible to Draazy staff only.

Daily checklist

Monitor

  • You have an unsaved draft banner: Resume or Discard it before starting another.
  • Properties, To verify, with the Awaiting owner chip: listings waiting on the owner.
  • Link opened chip: the owner opened the claim link but has not confirmed.
  • Reminded ×N on a row: how many nudges the owner has had.

Work on

  • Enter each new call or WhatsApp handoff through Details, Location, Pricing and Photos & Review.
  • Read the pending-listing warning before you submit, so you do not repeat a property.
  • After Send to Owner, press Send claim link on WhatsApp, then I've sent it.
  • Nudge owners who have not confirmed with the bell icon (Remind the owner on WhatsApp).

Desk and access

Use Admin → Post on Behalf (/admin/post-on-behalf) to create a listing for an owner who shared details by call or WhatsApp. You need the Post on behalf function (postOnBehalf:write); staff open it under /staff/post-on-behalf.

The listing is created under the owner, not under staff. If the mobile does not belong to an existing user, the backend provisions an owner account and audits both the user provision and property creation.

Wizard steps

Step Staff action
Details Capture owner name, 10-digit mobile, property type and the key facts (BHK for homes, carpet area). Take only the key facts on the call: the owner adds the rest and the photos when they confirm
Location Pick the locality, search the society on Google Maps (a pick sets its pin and pincode) and add the full address
Pricing Capture rent or sale price; deposit is required for rent only
Photos & Review Paste owner-provided photo URLs if supplied ("Add photo URL"), add Internal Notes on the Details step if needed, review, then Send to Owner

Choose For Rent or For Sale before entering details. The choice controls deposit and possession fields.

Validation rules

Field Rule
Owner mobile Must be 10 digits starting with 6, 7, 8 or 9
Owner name Required
Property type Required. Commercial also needs a type and a shell type; homes need BHK
Carpet area Required
Locality Required
Price Required; deposit also required for rent
Floor Cannot be greater than total floors
Land listings Require NA status and other rights; farmland sale also requires buyer eligibility
Photos Optional URL entries; the owner must have at least three photos, two labelled by room, before they can confirm

The browser autosaves a draft under dz_pob_draft_v2. Use Resume to continue or Discard to clear it.

Duplicate and plan warnings

The desk checks pending listings under the same mobile and shows an advisory warning ("This owner already has N pending listings. You can still continue if this is a different property."). It also checks the owner's listing allowance. Staff-posted creation is exempt from the freemium ceiling, but overage is a Listing Pass conversation before submission.

Do not ignore a pending-listing warning. Open Admin → Properties and confirm you are not recreating the same property.

Submission and owner handoff

  1. Review the generated listing title and all required fields.
  2. Click Send to Owner.
  3. On the success screen, click Send claim link on WhatsApp, press send in your WhatsApp, then click I've sent it. This is free: it goes from your own WhatsApp.
  4. To resend later, open the listing's review, pick Onboarding welcome under WhatsApp templates, and use Mark sent in the Communication log.
  5. Wait for owner confirmation before the listing goes live.

The owner confirmation endpoint records claim-link opened time and owner confirmation time. Publication is blocked while a staff-posted listing still waits for owner confirmation.

The owner confirms from the listing wizard, which holds the listing to the same bar as a new post: every required detail and at least three photos. The more you capture on the call, the less the owner has to fill in.

Use internal notes for call details that matter to reviewers. The listing creation route has no notes field, so the desk saves notes to the listing timeline after creation.

Never do in post on behalf

  • Do not use your own mobile as the owner mobile.
  • Do not bypass owner confirmation for a staff-posted listing.
  • Do not create a second pending listing when the same mobile already has the same property waiting.
  • Do not promise the listing is live after Send to Owner; it still needs owner confirmation and review.
  • Do not paste private call notes into public listing fields.

Related

  • Verification SLAs
  • Ownership and badges
  • Drafting desk and service queues

articles.title: Support chats
articles.summary: How staff use the Support chats inbox: one chat per customer, who owns it, what each desk can see, and when to raise a service ticket.
articles.html:
Important

Internal runbook. Visible to Draazy staff only.

Daily checklist

Monitor

  • Waiting on us count on /admin/support: customers whose last message nobody has answered. A teal dot marks unread rows.
  • On desktop, the round chat button bottom-right shows the same waiting count on every staff page.
  • If the inbox says "We could not read the support chats", try again. That is not an empty inbox.

Work on

  • Work Waiting on us first.
  • Check Mine for chats you own that the customer has answered.
  • Resolve a chat when the customer has what they need.

Desk and access

Open Support chats (/admin/support; staff use /staff/support). What you see depends on your functions, in Team & access:

You hold You see
Support, or you are a manager or admin Every chat and every topic, including General. You can assign, resolve and raise service tickets
Listing moderation or Property verification Property topics only
Flatmates Flatmate topics only
A service desk (Rent Agreement, Property & Legal, and so on) Request topics for your own desks only
KYC review Identity topics only
Refunds Payment topics only

A desk-scoped view has no Mine tab, no Assign to me or Resolve, and its About filter lists only your topics. Sending a reply outside your topics fails with "This chat topic is outside your desk." Home Loans alone does not open the inbox.

One chat per customer

Each customer has one continuous chat. Every message is tagged with what it is About: a property, a flatmate post, a service request, an identity check, a payment, or General. There is no separate thread per question.

Tab Shows
Waiting on us The customer spoke last on at least one topic
Mine Chats assigned to you that are not resolved (full access only)
All Every chat in your scope, newest first

The About filter narrows any tab to Property, Flatmates, Requests, Identity, Payments or General. Each row shows the customer, time, a preview ("Support:" when we spoke last), the About chip, a Waiting chip, and Handled by {name} or Unassigned.

Working a chat

Open a row. The header shows the customer's name and masked mobile, a status chip (Waiting on us, Answered or Resolved) and who handles it.

  • Case chips list the customer's open cases. Tap one to reply about that case.
  • Reply about sets what your reply is about. It defaults to what the customer asked about last.
  • Enter sends; Shift+Enter adds a line. Replies can be up to 4,000 characters.
  • Timeline dividers show when the topic changed.

A reply about a property review, a flatmate post or a service request lands on that case too, so the desk that owns it sees it.

Who owns a chat

The first full-access replier becomes the owner. Everyone else sees Handled by {name}. A desk answering its own topic does not take the whole chat. To take over, press Take over (shown instead of Assign to me when someone else owns it).

Resolve and reopen

Resolve marks the chat resolved and clears unread. It also resolves the customer's open support tickets behind the chat, except identity appeals and disputes, which stay with their desk. There is no reopen button: when the customer writes again the topic goes back to Waiting on us. A staff reply on a resolved chat makes it Answered.

From a desk

Property review, flatmate review, the service queues and the rent-agreement desk show a Chat with customer button (with a count of messages). It opens the customer's chat at that case: a docked window on desktop, or the inbox on a phone. If it says "Couldn't reach this customer's support chat.", press Retry.

The dock (desktop only) opens up to three chat windows, which you can minimise or close. It is hidden on the inbox page itself.

Chat, desk case, service ticket

Thing Purpose Lives in
Support chat People talking. No priority, SLA or money /admin/support and the dock
Desk case Work with a decision: approve a listing, verify identity, draft an agreement, refund Its own desk
Service ticket Internal lead for a service team. The customer is never told Customer tickets tab on that desk

To raise one, press Service ticket in the chat header (full access only), pick the team, write a subject and optional note, then Create ticket. See Chats, tickets and escalation.

Never do

  • Never approve or promise a refund in a chat. Send it to Refunds desk or the service desk.
  • Never put staff-only notes in a reply. The customer reads it.
  • Never share another user's contact details.
  • Never move the conversation to WhatsApp or personal email.
  • Never tell a customer nobody is waiting when the inbox failed to load.

Related

  • Chats, tickets and escalation
  • Staff desks at a glance
  • Service queues
  • Identity review

articles.title: Drafting desk and service queues
articles.summary: How staff work rent-agreement drafting and other paid service-request queues.
articles.html:
Important

Internal runbook. Visible to Draazy staff only.

Daily checklist

Monitor

  • Overdue button count: rent-agreement cases past their desk target.
  • SLA cell on rent agreements: Due in turns warning at 2 h left, then Overdue by; Customer's turn and Waiting for tenant details have no desk timer. An approved case also shows register by a date.
  • Targets: pick up within 4 h, first draft 48 h, revision 24 h, registration 7 days.
  • To pick up count. Other desks have no SLA cell: row age shows "due soon" (amber) after 24 h and "overdue" (rose) after 72 h.

Work on

  • Work Overdue rent agreements first, then To pick up with Take case.
  • Rows marked Our move are yours to act on. With customer rows wait on the customer.
  • Finish first drafts and changes-requested revisions before the targets run out.
  • Upload the registered copy for approved cases, then run Registration check.

Desk and access

Each service is its own sidebar entry: Rent Agreement at /admin/rent-agreement, and Property & Legal, Interior & Renovation, Packers & Movers and Property Valuation at /admin/legal, /admin/interior, /admin/packers and /admin/valuation. Old /ops/drafting-desk?type=… and /ops/<desk> bookmarks redirect to the matching page.

A staff member sees only the service desks they were granted (Rent Agreement needs the rental desk function), under /staff/…. Admins and managers see every desk.

Queue controls

Control Use it for
To pick up / My cases / In progress / With customer / Closed / Cancelled Queue tabs with live counts (My requests on the other desks). Closed is completed work; Cancelled holds cases cancelled by the desk or withdrawn by the customer
Overdue Rent-agreement SLA breaches only
All / Today / 7d / 30d Date chips that narrow the list by when the request came in
Name, mobile or request id Server-side search
Customer tickets The desk's tickets tab (needs tickets:read)

The list is paged at 20 rows. A failed load is shown as an error, not as an empty queue.

On the Rent Agreement desk each row shows an Our move, With customer or Closed chip, a Yours chip on cases you hold, and a Step n of 7 line. The seven stages are Paid, Picked up, Papers verified, Draft shared, Approved, Registered and Police intimation. Inside a case, Next case jumps to the next one in the list. The Messages tab holds Chat with customer (the customer's support chat for that request), and a Payment tab appears on paid cases with the Refunds section. An Activity tab shows the history.

Home Loans is a ticket-style desk without this case window. Work it from its own request list.

Status states

Status How it is reached Staff action
awaiting-payment Paid service created before payment settles Not in the working queue
new Paid or free request ready for ops Take it
assigned Take case (rent agreement) or Take this request (other desks) Start work
in-progress Status set to in-progress Continue work
draft-shared Share draft succeeds Customer reviews
changes-requested Customer rejects the draft Revise or cancel
action-required Send back for correction Owner or tenant fixes it; their Done returns it to in-progress
approved Customer approves the draft Upload final or registered copy
completed Final document uploaded Run the registration check if rental
cancelled Staff cancel with a reason Terminal

Only assigned, in-progress, and cancelled are directly staff-settable. draft-shared, approved, changes-requested, action-required, and completed are created by draft upload, customer decision, send-back, and final upload.

Age and SLA targets

Rent agreements carry server SLA due dates:

State Target
new Pick up within 4 hours
assigned / in-progress First draft within 48 hours
changes-requested Revision within 24 hours
approved Registration within 7 days
draft-shared / action-required Customer's turn; no desk timer

The SLA cell shows Due in, Overdue by, or Customer's turn from that SLA; Waiting for tenant details shows when the tenant has not yet filled their part. It turns warning when two hours or less remain. For an approved rental the statutory registration deadline (four months from approval) is also shown as register by, with a warning in the last 30 days. Non-rental queues fall back to age colouring: amber after 24 hours and rose after 72 hours while not completed or cancelled.

Rent-agreement document procedure

  1. Open the case. The rail shows the next step and whose move it is; the stage bar shows how far the case has come. Read Parties and Property & terms.
  2. Use Documents to verify every required paper. If the checklist cannot load, retry before asking the customer for anything.
  3. Check Overlap check. If another paid agreement overlaps the same flat and months, confirm the old tenancy ended or this is a replacement before drafting.
  4. Use Priced terms only for rent, deposit, term, increment, or registration-area corrections. The customer must accept; any higher fee is paid before the draft goes out.
  5. Use ID numbers → Reveal only when you hold the matter. Hide or close the modal when done; reads and refusals are audited.
  6. Share the draft only after the checklist is verified and no priced-term amendment is open.

Corrections

  • Fix it yourself. While you hold the case and no draft is out with the customer, every card under Licensor, Licensee, Property and Terms has Edit, including passport, visa/OCI and FRRO details. List rows (furniture, deposit payments, occupants) can be added and removed there. Saving tells the customer how many details changed, with your note. Rent, deposit, term, escalation and registration area go through Priced terms.
  • Fix a PAN or Aadhaar. Take the case first (admins too), then on ID numbers, Reveal and Correct on the party. Every party on the form is listed, even one whose numbers were never recorded. The customer is told an ID was corrected; the audit records who changed which party, never the number. Renaming a party on the form keeps their numbers.
  • Send it back. Only for what you cannot do yourself: a fresh copy of a paper, or an answer only the customer has. Use Send back for correction in the rail, pick the side, tick the papers to upload again and/or ask your question. They get an in-app notification (WhatsApp when the template is set) and an amber banner on their tracker with an upload for each paper. Only the side you asked can mark it Done, and only once every ticked paper is uploaded again; that returns the case to in-progress, with their reply in the thread. Review the new copies on the checklist as usual.

Draft checks and customer decision

Before Share draft, tick every drafting check: identity numbers, title proof, POA, address, and terms. The server refuses rent-agreement drafts without these checks.

A draft you share goes straight to the customer; no second operator checks it first. Share it only after the checklist is verified and every drafting check is ticked.

Registration and trust evidence

After the customer approves the draft, upload the registered copy with the Sub-Registrar record: document number, Sub-Registrar office, registration date (not in the future) and GRAS GRN. The registered copy can be up to 2 MB; drafts and customer papers up to 1 MB.

For Leave & Licence Article 36A pricing, the code charges stamp duty from rent, term, non-refundable deposit, and 10% of refundable deposit per chargeable year; registration is ₹1,000 urban or ₹500 rural, plus ₹300 handling. Correct the registration area with Priced terms before sharing a draft if the locality body is wrong.

After completion, use Registration check:

  1. Open the registered copy.
  2. Compare it with the approved draft and the registration record.
  3. Confirm each tenant only if the number was OTP-verified and you did not upload the copy. A colleague with the registration-check permission has to confirm it.
  4. Use Not on the copy when the tenant is absent or not OTP-verified.

Confirmed registered tenancies can become trust evidence. Typed tenant numbers that were never OTP-confirmed cannot earn that badge.

Police intimation

Police intimation is the last stage and completes on its own when you upload the registered copy. Registering on the IGR portal shares the tenant's details with the police, so there is nothing to file or record.

Refunds and cancellation

Use Refunds only on paid rent-agreement requests. The holder asks for a refund; a manager approves it, and the manager alerted in their notifications opens the case from there. The refund also waits on the admin Refunds page under the Rent agreement filter, where a manager can decide it too. Staff cannot approve or reject a refund, only withdraw one they asked for, and never once the request is cancelled. A manager can approve a refund they asked for, including one their own cancel raised. Before duty is paid, everything paid can be refunded. After GRAS duty is paid, only the refundable balance beyond statutory charges can go back.

Use Cancel request only before completed or cancelled. A cancellation reason is required and is sent to the customer. Cancelling a paid rent agreement raises a refund of what is still refundable for a manager to approve. The customer is told it is waiting for approval, not that it is sent. If a refund was already waiting, the cancel keeps it rather than adding a second one.

What never to do

  • Never ask for documents when the checklist failed to load
  • Never reveal identity numbers on a matter you do not hold
  • Never share a rent-agreement draft with unverified papers
  • Never approve your own registered copy
  • Never refund a cancelled customer by hand: approve the refund the cancel raised
  • Never ask the owner or tenant to file police intimation separately
  • Never use registration or docs_review as a staff status

  • Verification SLAs
  • Identity review
  • Ownership and badges

articles.summary: How staff work non-rent-agreement service requests on their service desk pages.
articles.html:
Important

Internal runbook. Visible to Draazy staff only.

Daily checklist

Monitor

  • To pick up count on your desk.
  • Row age: amber ("due soon") after 24 h, rose ("overdue") after 72 h while the request is open.
  • My requests: what you hold right now.
  • Customer tickets count, if the tab shows for you. These are internal service tickets raised by Support, not customer chats.
  • Ignore Overdue here: it only covers rent agreements and finds nothing on these desks.

Work on

  • Work To pick up, taking rose and amber rows first.
  • Press Take this request before you reveal identity numbers or upload files.
  • Check Documents; if the checklist failed to load, retry before asking the customer for anything.
  • Move My requests forward with Share draft and Chat with customer.

Desk and access

Open your service from the sidebar: Property & Legal (/admin/legal), Interior & Renovation (/admin/interior), Packers & Movers (/admin/packers) or Property Valuation (/admin/valuation). Each desk is its own function (services:read / services:write); staff see only the desks they were granted and open them under /staff/…. Admins and managers see every desk.

Legacy /ops/legal, /ops/interior, /ops/packers, and /ops/valuation bookmarks redirect here with the matching desk filter.

Current desk types

Filter Current label
legal Property & Legal
interior Interior & Renovation
packers Packers & Movers
valuation Property Valuation

Home Loans (/admin/home-loans) has no service requests: it is the loans board of internal service tickets. See Chats, tickets and escalation.

Queue controls

Control Use it for
To pick up / My requests / In progress / With customer / Closed / Cancelled Stage tabs with live counts; My requests is what you hold
Customer tickets The desk's internal service-ticket tab (needs tickets:read)
Date chips Narrow the list by how recently the request was filed
Name, mobile or request id Search requester or request
Refresh Re-read the current page

The Overdue toggle is tied to rent-agreement SLA data and finds nothing on these desks. Rows use age colouring only: amber after 24 hours and rose after 72 hours while still open.

Status states

Status What it means
new Request is ready for ops
assigned A staff member owns it
in-progress Work is underway
draft-shared A deliverable was shared with the customer
changes-requested Customer asked for changes
action-required The desk asked the customer to do something before work continues
approved Customer approved the draft
completed Final document uploaded
cancelled Terminal cancellation

Staff may set only assigned, in-progress, and cancelled. Use Share draft to reach draft-shared; customer approval reaches approved; Upload registered copy completes the request even when the uploaded file is a final service document rather than a legal registration.

Working procedure

  1. Open the row and read the summary fields.
  2. Use Take this request before handling identity numbers or uploading files.
  3. Read Documents. If the checklist fails, retry before asking the customer for anything.
  4. Use Files on this request to open customer uploads and previously shared deliverables.
  5. Use Drafting workflow → Share draft when the customer needs to review a deliverable.
  6. Use Chat with customer for customer-visible updates. It opens the customer's support chat at this request.
  7. Use Internal notes for staff-only context.
  8. Use Cancel request only with a clear reason; the customer is notified.

Documents and files

The checklist is folded from service metadata and request documents. It is read-only except where the rent-agreement workflow adds verification buttons. For non-rental desks, treat it as the list of what exists and what is missing.

Do not call a failed checklist an empty checklist. The screen’s failure text is deliberate: a failed read means the system does not know what was filed.

Identity numbers

The Parties' identity numbers panel can appear on any service request, but it is only useful when numbers were recorded. Reveal only after taking the request. Closing the modal or opening another matter clears the numbers from component state, and the server audits allowed and refused reads.

Cancellation

completed and cancelled are terminal. For every other status, cancellation requires a reason. The reason is sent as a customer-visible message and a cancellation notification.

What never to do

  • Never work a matter under another holder’s name
  • Never treat a load failure as no documents filed
  • Never reveal identity numbers before taking the request
  • Never invent a loans queue from this screen
  • Never use rent-agreement-only actions such as overlap, refunds or registration check on these desks

Related

  • Drafting desk and service queues
  • Support chats
  • Chats, tickets and escalation
